question: Dospelý bocian biely je takmer nemý, chýba mu poriadny hlas. Ako sa teda bociany na hniezde zdravia a dorozumievajú?
source_excerpt: communicate using loud bill clattering (rapid opening and closing of the beak) and low hissing sounds

extra.why_interesting: Every Slovak has seen storks on chimneys and village poles, but few realise the bird is almost mute. The player assumes it calls like other birds, then remembers the familiar 'klepotanie' sound and works it out.
extra.verification_notes: White storks are nearly voiceless as adults and use bill-clattering for greeting and communication at the nest (https://kent.wildwoodtrust.org/animals/white-stork/).

explanation: Bocian zakloní hlavu dozadu a rýchlo cvaká zobákom, takže to znie ako drevená rapkáč. Hlasno pípať a syčať vedia len mláďatá.

question: Ktorý lesný vták si na jeseň zakopáva do zeme tisíce žaluďov, mnohé z nich potom už nenájde, a tak nevedomky vysádza nové duby?
source_excerpt: in a year of high seed crop, a single Jay can scatterhoard thousands of acorns in a single season

extra.why_interesting: People think of forests as being planted by wind or by foresters, not by a forgetful bird. The stem offers footholds (common forest bird, acorns, burying) so a player can reason toward the jay, a bird every Slovak has heard screeching in the woods.
extra.verification_notes: Jays scatterhoard thousands of acorns per season and thereby promote oak recruitment; no contradicting source or newer development found (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10336-021-01892-y).

explanation: Jedna sojka dokáže za jeseň ukryť aj niekoľko tisíc žaluďov a nezabudnuté zásoby vyklíčia. Aj jej latinský názov glandarius znamená 'žaluďová'.
